definitions.explanation: In Japanese school grammar, the smallest natural unit a sentence breaks into when spoken: one content word plus any particles or auxiliaries attached to it.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{文節|ぶんせつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{区切|くぎ}って→区切る：11850_kugiru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please divide this sentence into bunsetsu.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三|みっ}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{文節|ぶんせつ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦できている→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: 「私は本を読む」 is made up of three bunsetsu.

examples.japanese: {文節|ぶんせつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{切|き}れ{目|め}→切れ目：20720_kireme⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧」⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れて→入れる：01098_ireru⟧みる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦どこ→どこ：00539_doko⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{区切|くぎ}る→区切る：11850_kugiru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦わかりやすい→わかりやすい：09582_wakariyasui⟧。
examples.english: If you try inserting ね where you think a bunsetsu ends, it is easy to see where to divide.

notes:
USAGE:
A term of school grammar ({学校文法|がっこうぶんぽう}). The usual test is to insert ⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ / {本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ / ⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧.
